## Contact Forces Only Push

<!-- STEP id="only-push" -->
Blocks touching each other can only push — never pull.

It's the same rule as a normal force: a surface can shove something away from itself, never drag it along.

<!-- STEP id="b-carries-c" -->
## B Carries C Along

Push B toward C: B presses into C, so B pushes C forward too.

But B is moving away from A — there's nothing left to keep pushing A.

<!-- STEP id="a-left-behind" -->
## A Has No Force On It At All

Once B separates from A, no force acts on A whatsoever.

A doesn't lag behind a little — it doesn't move even a little. It just stays exactly where it was.

<!-- STEP id="the-numbers" -->
## Two Blocks, Not Three

$$a_{B,C} = \frac{F}{m_B + m_C}$$

**B and C move together. A's acceleration is exactly zero.**
